transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you here — is there something specific you'd like to talk about or get help with?

Well, I guess I came in because I’ve just been worrying about… everything, really. Work things, like clients and the market — which is always unpredictable, you know, especially in real estate — and then I go home and it’s my family, money, whether we made the right choice moving to the condo. 

I mean, the condo is fine, it’s actually a nice place, but I’ll find myself thinking, “Was that a mistake?” even when nothing has really happened. It just feels like my worry is bigger than the situation calls for, if that makes sense.
How often do you find yourself feeling this way — is it most days, or does it come and go?

It’s… I’d say most days, honestly. It comes up in different forms, but it’s like my mind just finds something to latch onto — a client issue, the market shifting, whether my family’s okay, money, and then somehow I’m back to questioning the condo move again.

Which is silly, because the condo is nice, and we picked it for good reasons, but I still go around and around with it. So yes, it’s not constant every minute, but it’s there a lot, and it feels bigger than what’s actually happening.
When you’re feeling this way, do you notice any physical symptoms like restlessness, trouble sleeping, fatigue, or muscle tension?

Yeah, I do notice it physically, mostly in my neck and shoulders. By the end of the day they feel really tight, like I’ve been sort of bracing myself without realizing it.

And sometimes when I’m driving between listings — which, depending on the day, can be all over town — or even just sitting at my desk going through emails, I’ll suddenly realize my jaw is clenched. Like I’ve been holding it that way for who knows how long.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like you’re losing control?

I’m not sure I’d call it that, exactly. I mean, I get worked up and I’ll feel uncomfortable, but I don’t know that it comes on like a sudden attack or like I’m losing control.

Sometimes I’ll be in the middle of something, like trying to get to a showing on time, and traffic is ridiculous, and then my mind starts going — but that feels more like worry piling up than something that just hits out of nowhere. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had episodes like that, at least not the way you’re describing.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you try to focus on something else or tell yourself not to think about it?

Yes… that’s probably the part that bothers me most. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent, you don’t need to solve it right now,” and I really mean it in the moment.

But then one concern sort of leads into another, and suddenly I’m thinking about a conversation I had with a client, or whether I missed some small detail, or—honestly, sometimes it’s something that doesn’t even matter by the next day. And before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour replaying it when I’d meant to just let it go and move on.
How long have you been feeling this way — when did you first notice these worries and physical symptoms starting to interfere with your day-to-day life?

I’d say it really started getting in the way a little over a year ago… about a year and two months, maybe. It was after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo.

I mean, the move itself was supposed to simplify things, and in some ways it did — less upkeep, no yard, all of that — but after that, I started noticing the worrying wasn’t just normal “busy life” stuff anymore. It kind of followed me around during the day.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, along with the worrying?

I don’t know… not really in a clear way. I mean, I have days where I’m kind of tired of dealing with everything, and I’ll think, “Oh, I should go meet a friend or do something nice,” and then I end up checking emails or fussing over some little thing instead.

But I wouldn’t say I’ve completely lost interest in things. I still like seeing people, looking at houses, even just walking around a neighborhood and noticing what’s changed — that’s always been something I enjoy. Although, you know, neighborhoods change so fast now, sometimes I’ll drive through an area I used to sell in years ago and it’s like a whole different place.

So… I guess I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I feel down all the time, if that’s what you mean.
Have you had days where you feel down or sad most of the time, even when things aren’t particularly wrong?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. I have moments where I feel a little low or worn out, but not like the whole day is sad for no clear reason.

Sometimes I’ll wake up and feel kind of heavy, but then I’ll get into my routine, or I’ll see someone in the building, and it passes. Our condo has this lobby where people end up chatting longer than they mean to—honestly, I know more about some neighbors’ renovation plans than I ever expected to.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had many days where I’m sad most of the time when nothing’s wrong. It’s more that I get caught up in my head.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure out of the things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

I don’t think so… not in the sense that things feel flat or pointless. I still enjoy things when I actually do them.

Like, if I go out with a friend for coffee, I’m glad I went. Or if I’m looking at a house—honestly, I still get interested in the layout, the light, all those little details. Sometimes I’ll walk into a place and immediately think, “Oh, they should’ve opened up that wall,” even though nobody asked me.

I guess the harder part is getting myself to settle into enjoying something, if that makes sense. But once I’m there, I don’t think the pleasure is gone. It’s more like I get distracted or pulled into other things.
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or lacking energy, even when you haven't been doing anything particularly tiring?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’m exhausted for no reason, exactly. I do get tired, but usually I can point to something, or at least I think I can — running around, too much time on the phone, all the little back-and-forth things that come with work.

Although sometimes I’ll sit down and think, “Why am I so worn out?” and then I realize I’ve been mentally juggling ten things that don’t look like much from the outside. Real estate is funny that way — you can spend half a day doing what seems like nothing and somehow it takes it out of you.

But no, I haven’t really noticed a big lack of energy when I haven’t been doing anything tiring. It’s not something that stands out.
Do you find yourself getting anxious or upset about small issues or events that you used to handle without much concern?

Yes… I think that’s probably the main reason I came in, honestly. I seem to worry about everything now, and not always things that deserve that much attention.

Like with clients, I’ll be turning over some tiny detail from a showing, or wondering if the market is going to shift, or if I said something the wrong way. And then it’s my family, or money, or—this sounds silly—but even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. Which, I mean, it’s a perfectly nice place. The lobby is always freezing, but that’s not exactly a crisis.

It just feels out of proportion to what’s actually happening. Small things don’t stay small in my head the way they used to.
Have you noticed yourself getting more easily annoyed or irritated, even by small things that wouldn’t have bothered you as much before?

I’m not sure I’d say more irritated, exactly. I mean, I have moments—everyone does—but I haven’t noticed myself snapping at people or feeling constantly annoyed by little things.

Sometimes a small thing will get under my skin, like if someone is late to a showing or the elevator in my building is taking forever, but then again, elevators are their own little universe of frustration. I don’t think that’s new for me.

So… no, not really something that stands out as different.

Would you say that your worrying tends to be constant and not limited to specific situations or events, but rather spreads across many different parts of your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

Yes, I think that’s fair to say. It doesn’t stay in one box, if that makes sense. I came in because I feel like I worry about everything now — clients, whether I handled something right, the market, my family, money.

And then it drifts into things that should be settled, like the condo. I’ll find myself wondering if moving there was the right decision, even though there’s no real problem with it. Well, aside from the lobby being freezing, which I know I’ve mentioned, but still.

It just feels bigger than what’s actually happening. Like the worry spreads out and attaches itself to whatever is nearby.
When you're feeling especially worried or tense, do you notice symptoms like sweating, trembling, or a pounding heart?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve really noticed sweating or trembling in any obvious way.

The pounding heart thing… I mean, sometimes I’m aware of myself being tense, but I can’t say I’ve sat there thinking, “Oh, my heart is racing.” Usually I’m more caught up in whatever I’m worrying about — like replaying a phone call or thinking through some client issue — and then suddenly I’ve lost twenty minutes to it.

So… I don’t know that those physical symptoms are a big part of it, at least not that I’ve paid attention to.
